title: Calculating the Closing Payout on a Personal Checking Account
content:
The closing payout is the money reconciled from the Personal Checking account's own entries, less the closing charge and together with the closing interest.

**The money reconciled from the account's own entries** is every credit posted to it — deposits, refunds and goodwill entries, temporary credits, surcharge rebates and interest credits — less every debit posted to it, that is paid items, charges and take-back entries.

**The closing charge** owed for an account closed inside its opening window is taken out of the money paid out rather than booked as a separate entry on the account. An account closed later than its opening window owes no closing charge at all, and the closing payout is then the money reconciled from the account's own entries together with the closing interest alone; the opening window runs for the tier's early closure window in calendar days counted with the day after the account was opened as day one, and an account closed on the last of those days is still inside it. The closing charge is set at the tier's early closure charge, and is then taken at the level it was set, in full.

**The closing interest** is added to the money paid out rather than credited as a separate entry. It is the money reconciled from the account's own entries multiplied by the closing rate as an annual percentage, multiplied by the closing days and divided by three hundred and sixty-five, rounded half-up to the cent. The closing days are the days the account has been open, capped at one full statement cycle of 30 days. The closing rate is the base account rate of 0.02 percent.

The closing payout is taken in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up.

**Worked example on hypothetical inputs.** An account of a tier whose early closure charge is 25.00 and whose early closure window is 90 calendar days has been open 45 days and carries credits of 4300.00 and debits of 3300.00.

| Quantity | Hypothetical figure |
|---|---|
| Money reconciled from the account's own entries | 1000.00 |
| Days open against the tier's opening window of 90 calendar days | 45, so the account is closed inside the window |
| Closing charge owed | 25.00 |
| Closing days, the days open capped at 30 | 30 |
| Closing interest, at 0.02 percent a year on 1000.00 for 30 days | 0.02 |
| Reconciled money less the charge and with the interest | 975.02 |
| Closing payout, in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up | 975.00 |

Had the same account been open 200 days, it would sit later than the tier's opening window and owe no closing charge, so the figure carried into the rounding would be the reconciled money together with the closing interest alone. An account open 12 days would take 12 as its closing days rather than 30, the cap binding only above it.
